newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Peptech dives 17 pct on British news.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Peptech dives 17 pct on British news.

text.p: Shares in drug development firm Peptech Technology Ltd dived 14 cents or 17 percent to 68 cents in morning trade as Peptech announced it would postpone plans for a secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange.
Brokers and analysts said investors had hoped a London listing would raise Peptech's profile and potentially boost its price in the same way Memtec Ltd's U.S. listing sparked a major rally.
"The U.K. institutions don't seem very excited at all about Peptech," Macquarie Equities pharmaceuticals analyst Simon Jones said.
"One of the advantages about being listed in the U.K. is that there's a lot more institutions willing to invest in the biotechnology sector -- there's a lot more analysis," he said.
"People were perhaps expecting that listing to lift the profile and the market price and now that it's not going ahead, they're a bit disappointed," he said.
Earlier on Thursday, Peptech said it would postpone the secondary listing of its shares on the London Stock Exchange due to poor market conditions.

Peptech said a investor roadshow linked to the listing process had led Peptech's directors to believe that "it was not in the best interests of the shareholders and the company to proceed with the listing at this time."
It said it believed it had adequate cash to maintain development in key product areas.
Peptech, formerly Peptide Technology, said earlier this month that it planned to raise A$20 million from a private share placement in Europe linked with the listing.
Brokers and analysts said the expectation that Peptide would have now have to raise the A$20 million in Australia would also depress the share price.
"I imagine there's going to be a bit of a ceiling while there's still that belief that they need to raise some more money," Jones said.
Peptech's share price hit of low of 64 cents earlier in the day and by 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT) 526,608 shares had traded.
